_readme: PRODUCT TRUTH LEDGER — what the Leadkaun product actually ships.
This file exists because marketing copy drifted from product reality: the site
claimed assignment rules, round-robin routing, territory routing and an
'unassigned queue' in 8+ places, including a whole pillar and buyer guide. None
of it exists in the product. The Brain's canonical module list (00 s3) never
sanctioned it — it crept in, and nothing could catch it.
scripts/content-gate.mjs compiles the deny[] patterns below and fails the build
on any copy that claims an unshipped capability. evidence[] paths are asserted
to exist in the product repo, so if the product moves the ledger errors and
forces a re-review rather than silently blessing stale facts.
Deliberately NOT in data/pseo/: the gate lints every string in that directory
(this file must contain banned phrases verbatim), and upload-data-to-r2.js
syncs that directory to R2 — this is a build-time artefact, not page content.
status: shipped | partial | dark | not-shipped | roadmap | never-market | DISPUTED
dark = code exists but has zero production call sites
To change a status you must cite a product-repo path. No path, no change.

capabilities.label: Lead assignment
capabilities.claimable: An admin or manager can assign one lead at a time to a named rep.
capabilities.note: The import path never sets assigned_rep_id — imported leads arrive unassigned, and no surface lists them. There is no AssignmentRule or Territory model in prisma/schema.prisma.

capabilities.label: Learning Engine
capabilities.claimable: Read-only analytics — grade calibration against closed deals, close-time by grade, win rate by segment, and best contact hour. Every insight is sample-size gated and stays locked until there is enough data.
capabilities.note: signal-weights.ts is a static constant table and grade.ts thresholds are hardcoded literals. Nothing writes learned weights back into scoring; there is no learned-weight column in the schema. The engine reports what it observed — it does not act on it.
deny: the more you use it,? the better

capabilities.label: Signal-aware next-best-action engine
capabilities.claimable: Nothing. The shipped recommendation is a static grade-to-action map (A = Call now, B = Call today, C = Nurture, D = Low priority, E = Drop, F = Junk).
notClaimable: recommendations that adapt to conversation stage
capabilities.note: computeNextBestAction() in nba.ts has ZERO production call sites — only its own test file. Deliberately dark per an in-code comment: it stays off until there is adoption data to measure it against. If this ever ships, update this entry before writing copy about it.

capabilities.label: Recommendation adoption measurement
capabilities.claimable: We measure whether a recommendation was FOLLOWED — recommendation acceptance rate (accepted / shown), and the queue rank of the lead a rep contacts first (top 10 counts as following the queue).
notClaimable: we measure whether the recommendation worked
we track the outcome of every recommendation
capabilities.note: RAR (followed) ships. RSR (worked) is explicitly not computed — the read route says so. EXECUTED/OUTCOME events are now written but never aggregated into a success rate.

capabilities.label: WhatsApp logging
capabilities.claimable: Open the chat from Leadkaun via a wa.me link, have the conversation in your own WhatsApp, come back and record the outcome. The log then drives stage advancement, follow-up scheduling and rescoring.
notClaimable: reading or syncing your WhatsApp conversations
capabilities.note: Zero references to Gupshup, Twilio, 360dialog, WATI or Interakt anywhere in the product. It is a deep link plus a manual form. Capture is manual; everything downstream of the log is real and substantial.

capabilities.label: Scoring weights
capabilities.claimable: The weights are fixed, published and identical for every account — that is what makes a grade explainable and comparable. What you configure is the ICP that Fit is computed from.
capabilities.note: weight_overrides is dead per Brain 00 s4. You tune who a good customer is, not the maths behind it.

capabilities.label: Google Sheets sync
capabilities.claimable: Connect a Google Sheet and pull leads from it, optionally keeping it in sync so new rows arrive automatically.
capabilities.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-05, and the Brain doc is the stale one. Brain 00 s4 bans Sheets sync as 'non-functional, model never migrated' — but the migration landed 2026-07-24, ONE DAY before the Brain was authored, so it was written against a snapshot that had just gone out of date. Verified shipped: migration exists, sheetsSyncFn is registered at app/api/inngest/route.ts:20, /api/import/sheets has full POST/GET/DELETE, and the import page has connect + disconnect UI. Brain 00 s4 needs updating. Marketing copy about Sheets is CORRECT and stays.

capabilities.label: Mission Control / platform admin / impersonation
capabilities.note: Internal admin surface at admin.leadkaun.com. Never a marketing feature — Brain 00 s4. evidence[] points at a stable product file purely to keep the liveness check meaningful; this capability has no marketable surface.

capabilities.label: Lead scoring (Fit / Intent / Quality, A–F)
capabilities.claimable: Every lead graded A–F from three independent 0–100 scores — Fit (ICP match), Intent (signals, with decay), Quality (data reliability) — on a published threshold matrix. Quality below 20 forces F.

capabilities.label: Priority Queue
capabilities.claimable: One ranked list per rep that re-sorts as signals arrive. Reps work top-down instead of triaging.

capabilities.label: Intake Intelligence
capabilities.claimable: Before a single lead is imported, Leadkaun profiles the file — country and currency from phone shape, B2B vs B2C, industry inference, phone and email validity, in-file duplicates, missing fields — and shows you what is actually in it.
capabilities.note: Deterministic and explicitly non-LLM by design. Runs on a ~2k-row sample. ANALYSING is SYNCHRONOUS today — the schema comment says 'async-ready; today it's synchronous'. Never imply background processing.

capabilities.label: Import readiness band
capabilities.claimable: Each uploaded file gets a readiness band — High, Medium or Low — from mapping confidence, completeness, contact quality and business context.
capabilities.note: The underlying weighted score is marked internal in the schema and is NOT customer-visible. Publishing it as tunable repeats the weight_overrides mistake. Market the band, never the number.

capabilities.label: Score Evolution timeline
capabilities.claimable: An append-only timeline of every score change on a lead — grade, confidence and all three sub-scores frozen at each event, so you can see exactly why a grade moved.

capabilities.label: Confidence score
capabilities.claimable: Separate from the grade. The grade says how good a lead is; confidence says how much we actually know about it — an 8-field weighted completeness read with a prioritised enrichment checklist.
capabilities.note: Computed on demand, not stored on Lead; snapshotted onto score events.

capabilities.label: Data freshness
capabilities.claimable: Five ageing bands on every lead, so a list you bought six months ago does not look new the day you import it.
notClaimable: we know when the lead was originally collected
capabilities.note: When source collection date is absent, freshness is inferred from import date. Do not claim knowledge of true collection time.

capabilities.label: Daily Execution Score
capabilities.claimable: A time-of-day-aware daily score of whether the team is actually working the queue, with a mid-afternoon manager alert when it falls behind.
capabilities.note: Models a 09:30–19:00 IST workday. Weights are developer-tunable named exports, NOT customer-tunable.

capabilities.label: Offline signal logging
capabilities.claimable: A rep on a patchy connection can still log a call or WhatsApp outcome — it queues locally and syncs when the connection returns.
capabilities.note: It queues SIGNAL LOGS, not the whole application. Never say the app works offline.

capabilities.label: Win/loss attribution
capabilities.claimable: When a deal is marked won or lost, the lead's full scoring state is frozen at that moment — grade, sub-scores and reason — so you can go back and ask whether the grades actually predicted the outcomes.
capabilities.note: WinAttribution model plus an outcome_snapshot JSON frozen at decision time. This snapshot is what makes the Learning Engine's calibration honest — it compares against state as it was, not as it is now.
